Patient_population: Pediatric high-risk neuroblastoma with at least partial response after first-line multimodality treatment
Mechanism: GD2 binding; antibody-dependent and complement-dependent cytotoxicity
Administration: IV infusion for 4 consecutive days per cycle; up to 5 cycles; combined with GM-CSF IL-2 and isotretinoin
Efficacy_evidence: Randomized Phase III trial demonstrated improved event-free and overall survival with dinutuximab-based immunotherapy plus isotretinoin compared with isotretinoin alone in high-risk neuroblastoma.
Major_safety_risks: Severe neuropathic pain; infusion reactions; capillary leak; hypotension; neuropathy
Limitations: Repeated prolonged infusions; supportive care burden; significant pain and toxicity
Evidence_notes: Clinical efficacy was established for a dinutuximab-containing combination regimen in a randomized post-consolidation trial; direct comparisons with single-arm CAR-T studies in relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma are not valid due to differences in trial design, patient populations, and efficacy endpoints.

Patient_population: Age 1 year and older and adults with relapsed/refractory high-risk neuroblastoma in bone or bone marrow and partial/minor response or stable disease after prior therapy
Mechanism: GD2 binding; immune-mediated tumor cell killing
Administration: IV on days 1, 3 and 5 of cycle with GM-CSF; repeated cycles
Efficacy_evidence: Accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response
Major_safety_risks: Severe neuropathic pain; infusion reactions; neurotoxicity including transverse myelitis and RPLS
Competitive_strengths: Approved option in defined relapsed/refractory bone/bone marrow setting
Limitations: Restricted labeled disease setting; confirmatory clinical benefit required; pain and infusion burden
Evidence_notes: No head-to-head efficacy comparison with dinutuximab or CAR-T

Patient_population: Children with high-risk metastatic relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma
Mechanism: Engineered autologous T cells target GD2; inducible caspase-9 safety switch
Administration: Patient-specific cell manufacture; lymphodepletion and CAR-T infusion
Efficacy_evidence: Final phase 1/2 trial: ORR 66% (21/32 with measurable disease); 5-year OS 42.67% in trial cohort
Major_safety_risks: Cytokine release syndrome; ICANS including grade 3 events requiring safety-switch activation
Competitive_strengths: Potential durable response; CAR-T persistence; built-in safety switch
Limitations: Small nonrandomized study; manufacturing complexity; uncertain generalizability
Evidence_notes: Trial cohort n=35; 19 additional hospital-exemption recipients reported separately; avoid cross-trial rankings

Patient_population: Preclinical GD2-positive malignancy models including neuroblastoma
Mechanism: Anti-GD2 single-chain variable fragment linked to 4-1BB/CD3-zeta signaling
Administration: Research-stage engineered T cells; no established clinical regimen
Efficacy_evidence: Preclinical neuroblastoma cytotoxicity and xenograft antitumor activity; no verified neuroblastoma clinical response rate for this construct
Major_safety_risks: Human safety profile not established for this construct
Competitive_strengths: Distinct CAR engineering and translational intellectual property
Limitations: Preclinical evidence cannot establish clinical efficacy or safety
Evidence_notes: Do not conflate St. Jude construct with Italian GD2-CART01 trial

Patient_population: Children and young adults with relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma or osteosarcoma
Mechanism: Engineered GD2-targeted autologous T cells; includes safety-switch evaluation
Administration: Lymphodepleting chemotherapy followed by GD2CART infusion
Efficacy_evidence: Clinical activity under investigation; no established comparative efficacy estimate
Competitive_strengths: US-based clinical translational comparator with persistence objectives
Limitations: Phase 1; trial listed as suspended for safety-data review as of August 2026
Evidence_notes: Registry status is time-sensitive; verify before publication
